headline: Feds, Ontario offering Stellantis 'aggressive package' to keep Brampton auto plant open
briefing: Top stories right now: Feds, Ontario offering Stellantis 'aggressive package' to keep Brampton auto plant open; E-mail services restored to Toronto hospitals after Microsoft outage caused some disruptions; and Chris Van Hollen rules out 2028 presidential bid as challenge to take Senate leadership gains support – US politics live.

keyDates.label: New municipal term; Israeli cabinet meets
keyDates.why: Ontario councils and the appointed regional chairs begin their four-year term, Israel's security cabinet meets after ordering readiness for a possible Iran strike, and the Southeast Asian summit Carney is attending opens in Manila.

keyDates.label: OSAP bill expected
keyDates.why: Ontario is expected to table its legislation on student aid at private career colleges when the legislature sits Monday.

keyDates.label: APEC summit; Alaska ranked-choice count
keyDates.why: Carney meets Xi in Shenzhen on Nov. 18–19, and Alaska tabulates its Peltola–Sullivan Senate race.

keyDates.label: Senate Democrats pick a leader
keyDates.why: Democratic senators vote by secret ballot between Chuck Schumer and challenger Chris Van Hollen for majority leader.

keyDates.label: Bank of Canada and Fed rate decisions
keyDates.why: Both central banks decide the same day; the Bank of Canada has said more hikes are possible.

keyDates.label: Stellantis default deadline
keyDates.why: The 30 days Ottawa gave Stellantis on Nov. 12 to repay subsidies or reverse course run out, after which the government says it will sue.

stories.headline: Feds, Ontario offering Stellantis 'aggressive package' to keep Brampton auto plant open
stories.summary: TORONTO — A day after threatening to sue Stellantis to recoup federal cash given to the automaker, Industry Minister Mélanie Joly says she's still hopeful she can prevent the company from selling its Brampton, Ont., assembly plant to Roshel.
